title: Guards, lazy loading and preloading strategies

videos.script:
The router can do more than draw a page for an address. It can ask first, and it can wait to fetch code until the code is needed.

{{guards}} A guard is a question the router asks before a navigation. You write one that sends an unknown course to the not-found page. And you learn what a guard is not. It protects nothing, because the server still has to refuse.

{{leaving}} Another guard asks before a half-filled form is left, so typing is never thrown away without a word.

{{lazy}} Then the course area moves into a chunk of its own, downloaded only when a course is opened.

{{providers}} You count how many instances a service on a route really has. The answer is one, for good.

{{preloading}} Preloading fetches the lazy chunk while the first page is being read.

{{defer}} And defer does the same for a part of a template, with one surprise from the dev server.
